verdict.rationale: New Relic documents NRQL, a SQL-like query language over its data, and a logs UI that can filter by text or other attributes. That is direct but thin support for ad-hoc filtering. Nothing in the pack addresses grouping by high-cardinality fields, or whether querying works without pre-aggregation or indexes. One community report describes metric-name explosions from high-traffic unique URLs, which suggests cardinality limits on the metrics side. missing for 10: explicit group-by/facet documentation, documented support for high-cardinality attributes like user or request IDs, confirmation that no pre-aggregation or indexing is required, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can group and filter by high-cardinality fields (user id, request id) without pre-aggregating or defining indexes first

citations.quote: New Relic Query Language (NRQL) is a SQL-like language for querying your New Relic data.
From the main logs UI page, you can see all your logs and then filter down to logs with specific text, or other attributes.
